perspective:
Bradley’s available information:

- He is a salesperson at the marketing firm; Katherine Lasiloo is his colleague and the Marketing Manager. He knows their professional relationship has had friction over sales vs. marketing strategy.
- In their meeting, he presented data and charts from the last five campaigns to argue that traditional sales methods were being sidelined. He heard Katherine say she saw his point but that the market is evolving, digital outreach cannot be ignored, online engagement is increasing, and they should analyze data together to integrate both approaches. He told her he was frustrated that proven methods were not properly considered.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared success stories from recent digital campaigns that she said significantly boosted engagement and sales. He heard her say the strategy targets the right audience with the right message and that she would walk him through the analytics and decision-making. He admitted his doubts and asked to understand more; Katherine said she was glad he was open and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- He proposed a joint strategy meeting. Katherine agreed, saying combining strengths could improve results and that they should schedule a time to brainstorm next steps.
- After the joint meeting, he prepared a board presentation draft integrating both traditional and digital ideas. He showed it to Katherine; she said it looked comprehensive and well thought out and praised his hard work. He said he was convinced the integrated approach would set them apart. Katherine said she was confident and suggested reviewing/fine-tuning once more.
- After the presentation and implementation, he thanked Katherine, said he learned from her and valued his growth, and proposed regular strategy sessions. He heard Katherine say the project had come to fruition, that his openness made the partnership successful, and that she agreed to regular sessions.
